items.text: I spent around 70 hours playing Assassin's Creed Odyssey, and I found the combat to be engaging, but not overly complex. If The Witcher 3's combat is more challenging, I'm willing to give it a try. Can you recommend any tips or strategies for a smooth transition from Odyssey's combat to The Witcher 3's?

items.text: I'm looking for some recommendations for open-world games with engaging storylines. I recently finished Assassin's Creed Odyssey, so I'm looking for something similar.
What's the difference between the gameplay and story of The Witcher 3 and Dragon Age: Inquisition?
I'm leaning towards The Witcher 3, but I'm worried about the combat being too challenging. How does it compare to Assassin's Creed Odyssey's combat in terms of difficulty and complexity?
I'm thinking of trying out some of the other games you mentioned, like Red Dead Redemption 2 or Horizon Zero Dawn. Can you tell me more about the storytelling and atmosphere in those games?
I'm interested in learning more about Horizon Zero Dawn's story and atmosphere. Can you tell me more about Aloy's journey and the world she inhabits?

That's a great list! I'll definitely check them out. I'm particularly interested in Ori and the Blind Forest and Gris. Have you got any recommendations for games similar to Celeste, which I also loved?

I'm really interested in Spelunky and Cuphead. I've heard great things about them. Do you have any recommendations for games similar to The Last of Us Part II, which I recently completed on both normal and hard difficulties?

I'm also curious about God of War (2018) and Horizon Zero Dawn. I've heard great things about them. By the way, do you think you can recommend some games similar to Assassin's Creed Odyssey, which I completed recently?

I'm also interested in checking out some gaming news and updates on the upcoming PS5 and Xbox Series X consoles. Can you tell me more about their release dates, specs, and any notable games that will be available at launch?

I'm actually considering getting a PS5, mainly because I've been a PlayStation fan for a while and I'm excited about the exclusive titles like Godfall and Spider-Man: Miles Morales. Plus, I've heard great things about the DualSense controller and the Tempest Engine for 3D audio. But at the same time, I'm also curious about the Xbox Series X and its features like Quick Resume and Smart Delivery. I might have to do some more research and compare the two consoles before making a final decision.
I'm looking for games with strong narratives, so I think I'll check out Uncharted 4 and God of War. I've heard great things about them. Have you got any info on their storytelling and characters?

I'm really excited to dive into these games. I've heard that the storytelling in Uncharted 4 is heavily influenced by films, and I'm curious to see how that translates to a gaming experience. Do you think the game's cinematic approach will make the story feel more immersive and engaging?

I'm glad you mentioned Uncharted 4's cinematic approach. It's definitely one of the game's strongest aspects. By the way, I've been thinking about my gaming habits lately, and I realized that I spent around 30 hours playing The Last of Us Part II on hard difficulty, which was a really challenging but rewarding experience. Do you think Uncharted 4's difficulty level is comparable to The Last of Us Part II's hard mode?

So, I'm curious about the other games you mentioned earlier, like Horizon Zero Dawn and God of War. How do their difficulty levels compare to Uncharted 4 and The Last of Us Part II? Are they more or less challenging?
I'd like to ask about God of War's combat mechanics. I've heard that the game's combat is more methodical and strategic compared to other action-adventure games. Can you tell me more about that?
I've played Hyper Light Drifter already, but I'm interested in Ori and the Blind Forest. What's the story behind it, and is it as emotionally investing as Celeste?

I see. So Ori and the Blind Forest has a more expansive open-world design compared to Celeste. That sounds appealing. Are there any other indie games that focus on exploration and discovery, similar to Ori, but with a stronger emphasis on storytelling and character development?

I'm more interested in games with a stronger focus on storytelling and character development. Can you tell me more about What Remains of Edith Finch and Firewatch? How do they compare to Celeste in terms of storytelling and emotional investment?

I'm interested in What Remains of Edith Finch. Since it's a shorter game, I'd like to know more about its replay value. Are there multiple endings or secrets to discover that would encourage me to play through the game again?

I'm interested in exploring more indie games with strong storytelling and character development. Are there any games that you would recommend that have a similar atmosphere and tone to What Remains of Edith Finch?

I found the normal difficulty to be a good balance between challenge and storytelling. I was able to focus on the narrative and characters without getting too frustrated with the gameplay. Speaking of which, I'm curious about the game's development process. How long did it take the developers to create The Last of Us Part II, and what was the most challenging part of its development?

That's really interesting. I didn't know it took them 5-6 years to develop the game. I can imagine the emotional storytelling part was a challenge, considering how emotional the game can be. By the way, have you got any recommendations for games with similar emotional storytelling, but maybe in a different setting or genre?

I haven't played any of those games, but I've heard great things about What Remains of Edith Finch and Firewatch. I think I'll give one of those a try. By the way, do you have any recommendations for gaming communities or forums where I can discuss games with other players and get more recommendations?

I think I'll check out ResetEra and Reddit's r/Games. I've heard good things about both communities, and they seem like great places to discuss games with other players. Thanks for the recommendations! By the way, I'm also interested in learning more about the gaming industry and staying up-to-date with the latest news and developments. Are there any good websites or YouTube channels you'd recommend for gaming news and analysis?

I think I'll start with Polygon and Kotaku for written articles, and then check out some YouTube channels like GameSpot and Jimquisition. I've heard great things about Jim Sterling's in-depth analysis and critique of the gaming industry. I might also give the Game Informer Show podcast a listen, as I've enjoyed their magazine in the past.

By the way, I've been thinking about getting a new gaming keyboard. Do you have any recommendations for good gaming keyboards, or any specific features I should look for?
